final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and mainly reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is partly persuasive on scope: the evidence supports aggregate operational readiness in general, and it does not prove a blanket release failure. But that is not enough for compliant_with_caveats on this record. A caveated outcome would require evidence that the caveat has actually been converted into a policy-bounded compliant state, such as approved mitigation, approved risk acceptance, or final disclosure language that satisfies the policy for the named launch use case. The record still shows the opposite: the customs-triage weakness remains below target, the mitigation remains incomplete and unapproved, and the current model-card draft appears inconsistent with the disclosure requirement. So the issue is not merely that the claim needed narrower wording; the unresolved compliance predicate remains unmet.
remaining_concerns: The logistics customs triage launch slice remains below target for a named launch use case, so a current material weakness may still exist.

The mitigation artifact is still only a draft and is missing required approval-grade elements, including at least an accountable owner and alert threshold; the policy standard also requires a review date and rollback criterion for approved mitigation.
There is no admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance for the unresolved customs-triage issue.
The current model-card draft says there are no known material limitations even though the record shows an unresolved question about whether this use-case limitation must be disclosed.

Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support general operational readiness, but they do not satisfy the separate policy predicate for certification when a named use-case limitation remains unresolved or undisclosed.
